tax_units._what: The shared tax-unit rules (tax_units.py), run on every survey's member list (roster_cps.py, roster_scf.py, roster_cex.py, roster_sipp.py). TAX_UNITS.md, section 4.
tax_units._reassign: CBO's reassignment pass (4c): true is CBO's default; false applies the first assignment only. The SCF and CEX (roster_scf.py, roster_cex.py) read it; the CPS's units (filing.py) follow cps.cbo_variant, 'cbo' (with the pass) or 'strict' (without), and tax_units.py run as a script takes --strict.
tax_units._npeu_split: The SCF's adults outside the primary economic unit: how the group's income is divided among them. equal: equally; moore: wages among those under 70 and Social Security and pensions among those 62 and over (Moore's rule). inheritance._what: Inheritances received this year, an SCF-only slot (since 3 November; John, 2 November; roster_scf.inheritances, build_scf.R, build_table.SCF_AMOUNTS). The SCF's up to three reported inheritances, trusts and gifts (gift_type left out); the year received is rounded to the nearest 5 in the public file (years that would round past the interview set to the survey year), so each counts as received in the wave's income year with the chance its year code carries (year_weights: {wave: {year code: chance}}; codes not listed have chance 0), by a uniform draw keyed by the wave, the household and implicate and the inheritance's position, seeded by salt. 2013-2022: the Estate-Tax-Distribution model's weights (src/house_obbba.R), calibrated to Gale and Sabelhaus (2024). 2025: Gale and Sabelhaus's rule (their section F: the chance that an inheritance with a rounded year code was received in the income year is 1.25 over the statistical years the code covers, the survey taken at mid-year): the 2025 wave's code 2025 holds 2023, 2024 and 2025 to the interview, 2.5 years, so 1.25 / 2.5 = 0.5; code 2020 (2018-2022) does not hold 2024. The value is the value when received, taken as income-year dollars (scratch explore/2026-11-03/scf2025/DECISIONS.md).

network._what: The network (model.py, SlotTransformer): width of each slot's vector, layers, attention heads, ffn (the width inside each layer's feed-forward block), dropout.

training._what: Training (train.py): seed (REBUILD_SEED overrides it), passes over the table (REBUILD_PASSES overrides it), batch (records per step; 512 since 26 October, 4,096 before: about 1,780 steps a pass, an hour of training on an H100), the learning rate's peak, warm-up passes and final share of the peak, weight_decay, the share of the table held back to measure the fit (holdback_share, holdback_seed), and how often the log reports (log_every_passes).
training._q_groups: Grouped weighting (qgroups.py, 26 October): each training record counts by its survey weight times q = records / weight within its group, the groups from bands: 12 band-AGI groups on the PUF (agi12), 5 band-income classes per wave on the SCF (income5); q = 1 on the CEX and CPS. null: q = 1 everywhere.
training._overfit_log: The overfitting diagnostic of 28 October (overfit_log.py, branch rebuild-overfit-diag): true writes slot_log.csv in the model folder, the loss per slot on the held-back records and on a fixed sample of training records each pass, and saves the network every 10 passes (<run>_p10 to _p70). Logging only, with random generators of its own: training is the same either way. false: no log, as installed.

translation._what: Translation (translate.py): one row per survey and variable it shares with the PUF; a variable not here is not shared. Every comparison is against the tax data for the survey's year: PUF filers other than dependent filers, weights scaled by SOI Table 1.6 (filing status x age), dollars grown per return with the item, and the CPS units of that year (or the nearest CPS year) weighted by their chance of not filing. items: the survey's columns, summed; an empty list is zero (an item the survey does not ask). Definition fixes: first_year (asked from this tax year; earlier years zero), part (positive: the positive part; loss: the size of the loss, stored positive), loss_cap. loss_cap: a definition fix, losses read as no more than this. Function 1, dollar_line (PUF-year dollars, grown to the survey's year per return): amounts within the line of zero keep their dollars; amounts beyond it get the tax data's amount at the same count from the top (losses: from the bottom); null is dollars throughout, 0 is rank throughout. Function 2, fill_in (fillin.py): the two-slot fill-in on function 1's bands, on any survey (since 28 October the SCF, the CEX, the CPS and the SIPP), with size_ranges (PUF-year dollars) where reporting rates are read, and optionally type_extra (categories added to this row's type: the SCF's Schedule E rest, the partnership flag); it conditions on its survey's variables with type_for_fill_in (and the survey year) less the row's own variable (wages has the fill-in and is in every other item's type). A row with first_year fills in from that year only. Default: dollars, no fill-in; a departure gives its reason. report_lines: the dollar lines (survey-year dollars) of the report's size ranges. rank_against (optional, since 27 October): function 1 (and since 28 October function 2) compares the survey's amount with the tax data's amount of the named PUF variable (a computed total), or the sum of a list of them, instead of the row's own, for a survey that reports only a total and puts it in one of the total's parts. match (optional, since 28 October): how amounts beyond the dollar line are put on the tax data's scale: "count" (the default; a line of zero only) by the same count from the top (losses: from the bottom); "percentile_from_top" (wages) by the same share of ALL units counted from the top, so a survey missing small holders leaves the tax data's smallest amounts to function 2; "percentile" (required with a line above zero) by the same percentile among the units beyond the line in each data set (the survey's unit at the p-th percentile of its units beyond the line gets the tax data's p-th percentile of its units beyond the line; equal amounts get one value), so the order of units is kept and the map is continuous at the line. less_traditional_deferrals (optional, since 28 October): a definition fix, the survey column of each unit's elective deferrals (traditional plus Roth; missing where the survey does not ask), whose traditional part (settings deferrals: x (1 - the Roth share)) is subtracted from the amount: the link wage.

cps._generation_year: Since 28 October generation draws each record's year of this survey from the year file's prior (survey_mix.py, TARGETS.md section 7), and this year is used only for the single-year maps map_<survey>_<year>, kept for frames without a year column.
cps._step1_dir: The filing stage's folder, inside the run's data folder (filing.py): the CPS's tax units and roster in <step1_dir>/units/ (roster_<year>_<cbo_variant>_nogq.csv.gz, which build_cps.R reads), the filing requirement in <step1_dir>/requirement/, the returns in <step1_dir>/<step1_out>/ and the checks in <step1_dir>/checks/. Shared with the PUF (translation table): married, dependents, the primary filer's age range, wages, and the exact ages of the primary filer and the spouse; shared with the CPS: the spouse's share of the couple's wages. SIPP only: each adult's tips in dollars, and whether that adult's tips are mostly from leisure and hospitality (tips_primary, tips_spouse, tips_lh_primary, tips_lh_spouse), drawn last at generation under the SIPP label at the record's own SIPP year; the tips' dollar map is that year's records, grown to the target year by SOI's wages per return with wages, as the CPS's childcare. The file's tips1 and tips2 are each person's drawn tips held to at most that person's wages (wages1, wages2: tips are part of wages, as on Form W-2), and tips their sum.
sipp._years: Reference years, chosen as the CPS's (settings cps.years): every other year from the PUF year to the last year with a release. 2015 is the 2014 panel's wave 3; 2017-2023 the annual releases of 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2024 (NOTES.md in paths.raw.sipp: the 2018 release in the older folder is truncated, this one is complete).
sipp._generation_year: Since 28 October generation draws each record's year of this survey from the year file's prior (survey_mix.py, TARGETS.md section 7), and this year is used only for the single-year maps map_<survey>_<year>, kept for frames without a year column.

sipp._mfs_salt: Separate returns: joint couples are split by the CEX's rule (tax_units.mfs_split, keyed draw with this salt, dependents with person 1) until their weight reaches SOI Table 1.6's separate returns.

deferrals._what: Elective deferrals to 401(k)-type plans (since 28 October; NEXT_STEPS.md, wages and pre-tax deductions). The SCF's elective deferrals are also an SCF-only slot (elective_deferrals), with the spouse's share of them (spouse_deferral_share), drawn at generation (none without wages, the share 0 unless married); in the file each person's are held to the file year's legal limit for their age and to their own wages, and each person's traditional part is Tax-Simulator's trad_contr_er1 and trad_contr_er2, with Medicare wages = wages plus both (dollars.py; decided 27 October).
deferrals._limits: 2012-2026 as published by the IRS (2024 $23,000 and a $7,500 catch-up; 2025 $23,500 and $7,500, the age 60-63 catch-up of SECURE 2.0 left out; 2026 $24,500 and $8,000). 2027-2035 (30 October, placeholders): the 2026 limit and catch-up grown 2.4% a year (about CBO's CPI-U projection) and rounded down to $500, as the law indexes them; 2036-2075 (4 November 2026, the long-run years) by the same rule.
deferrals._roth_share: Roth (box 12 codes AA, BB, EE) over all elective contributions (codes D, E, F, G, H, S plus the Roth codes), dollars, joint returns and non-joint returns: SOI W-2 statistics, Table 5.A of w2_all_2018.xls for 2012-2018 and Table 4.B of w2_t4_<year>.xlsx for 2019 and 2020 (paths.raw.soi_w2; all taxpayers 2019: $30.3 billion of $352.9 billion, 8.6%). Years after 2020 take 2020's.
deferrals._sipp_item: The SIPP's own contributions to 401(k), 403(b), 503(b) and Thrift Savings Plan accounts at the main employer, asked in the 2022 and 2024 releases (reference years 2021 and 2023); the earlier releases do not have it, so their units' deferrals are missing (not asked) and their link wage is gross wages.

filing._what: The CPS's filing stage (filing.py, filing_requirement.R; run.sbatch stage filing): every CPS tax unit's chance of filing, by the filing rule v4 (John, 24 October 2026): logit(chance) = a(age band of the head) + k x (a child under 17) + required x (r + s x log gross income, centred on the year's weighted median among required units + b x (business or farm income not zero)), required being the statutory filing requirement. The 11 settings (7 a's, k, r, s, b) are solved each year so that 11 targets hold exactly: non-filing heads and spouses in 7 age bands = CPS adults - adults on returns (SOI Table 1.6, age_shape's filing_adults) - dependents aged 15+ not filing their own return (group quarters left out, so zero); and the four shares below. Dependents' own returns: file if required to or with any wages. No outside filing model.
filing._child_share: Non-filing children under 17 as a share of the CPS's children under 17, every year: the 2015 share, (Census PEP under 17, 69,494,950, less the 2015 PUF's N24 on returns other than dependent filers, 67,354,355.8) / 69,494,950 = 2,140,594.2 / 69,494,950. Child credit counts are not used after 2015 because the age limit, the Social Security number rule and refundability changed (John, 23 October 2026).
filing._required_nonfiling_share: Non-filing household units among units required to file, every year: 11.19 million (Pub 5785 Table 3, required non-filing units, TY2014-16 average; research/state_weights/nonfiler_residual/resources/pub5785_table3_notfiler_units.csv) / 118.53 million required units in the 2015 CPS (by this stage's units and requirement). The 2015 run checks the ratio.
filing._income_share: The gross income of required non-filers as a share of all required units' gross income, every year: $409.4 billion (Pub 5785 Table 3, total income of required non-filers, TY2014-16 average) / $8,987.5 billion (required units' gross income, 2015 CPS). The 2015 run checks the ratio.
filing._business_share: Required non-filers with business or farm income (head and spouse, INCBUS + INCFARM, positive or negative) as a share of required non-filers, every year: 4.99 / 11.19 million (Pub 5785 Table 3, TY2014-16 average).
filing._mfs_salt: Separate returns: joint couples are taken in the order of a uniform keyed by unit id with this salt (tax_units.mfs_split) until weight x calibrated chance reaches SOI Table 1.6's separate returns / 2.
filing._age_shape: Adults on returns by age band (column filing_adults: SOI Pub 1304 Table 1.6 as the non-filer pool's residual anchor builds it) and Census PEP adults (pep_adults, used only in a check), per year; tracked in the repository.
filing._pep_children: Census PEP resident population under 17 and under 18 on 1 July of each tax year, the national sum of the state rows (SEX 0, ORIGIN 0, all races): 2015, 2017 and 2019 from the 2010-2020 intercensal estimates (sc-est2020int-alldata6.csv), 2021 and 2023 from Vintage 2024 (sc-est2024-alldata6.csv), both in /nfs/roberts/project/pi_nrs36/shared/raw_data/Census-PEP/ (manifest.csv gives the Census URLs). Used in the checks only (people by age, and the children's row of nonfilers_vs_targets).

ages._what: The primary filer's age range (ages.py). Step 0 for PUF records with no range: a logit prior from the return, calibrated to SOI Table 1.6 less the known-range weight in each filing status x AGI cell where at least min_missing_share of the weight has no range. Survey couples: the man is the primary, except the woman with a chance by the man's range that reproduces the PUF's female-primary share by range; same-sex couples, the older partner.

blindness._what: The blindness rule's PUF reading (since the second retrain of 29 October; John; build_non_micro_tables.puf_blind_rates, non_micro_imputations.blindness). On unmarried returns taking the standard deduction (single, head of household; not dependent filers) the deduction above the basic amount, in units of the additional amount for the aged or blind, is the number of extra boxes; blind = the boxes less one at 65 and over. The rates by age range where the return shows it go to resources/non_micro/puf_blind_rates.csv. The 2015 PUF's amounts: the basic standard deduction by filing status (1 single, 4 head of household) and the additional amount for an unmarried filer. whole_tolerance: how far from a whole number the boxes may be (97% of these returns are within it). Blindness was a PUF slot learned in pretraining on 29 October; it drew 2.95 million blind primary filers against 260 thousand boxes, so it is now a rule.

generation._what: The filer batch and the non-filer batch (generate.py says how). Since 26 October the AGI group label is preset on every filer record and everything else is drawn given it.
generation._label: label_records: the filer records over all pooled models (each draws an equal share), split across the 12 band-AGI groups (qgroups.py) in proportion to the PUF's records per group (about 18,400 at p99.99 and over, 30,500 at p99.9-99.99). Each record's group is preset; its weight is the group's 2015 PUF returns over the records drawn in it (1 / q). Every drawn record is kept; the share whose drawn bands fall in another group is only reported (label_check.csv). label_seed: the batch's draws (plus each model's seed_shift).
generation._scf_wave_seed: TARGETS.md section 7: each record's SCF wave is drawn with the shares in the target year's configuration (targets_config/<year>/prior.yaml, 'balance sheet'), by a random generator seeded by this and the batch's generation seed, so no other draw moves.
generation._survey_year_seeds: TARGETS.md section 7 (27 October): each record's CEX year, CPS year and SIPP year are drawn with the shares in the target year's configuration (prior, 'consumption', 'cps items', 'sipp tips'), each by a random generator of its own, seeded by the survey's number here and the batch's generation seed, so no other draw moves (as scf_wave_seed does for the SCF's waves).
generation._nonfiler_records: Step 2: the non-filer batch, drawn from the CPS label at the target year with the filing flag 0, no oversampling, every weight 1. Its number of records is the filer batch's (label_records) times the CPS's expected non-filers in the target year (sum of weight x (1 - filer_p)) over SOI's returns that year. nonfiler_seed fixes its draws.
generation._models: The trained models pooled into each year's file (TARGETS.md section 8): equal shares of every batch, each model with its own generation seeds (seed_shift added to every seed), record ids from k x 10,000,000 for model k. Train each with REBUILD_RUN set to its run name (and REBUILD_SEED to its seed). null draws from the run's own model alone, with today's seeds; set it to null for a fresh single-seed train-then-generate run. Three seeds, 20261017-19, since 28 October (John): the seed-20261016 network was a much worse fit (explore/2026-10-28/model_variability/RESULTS.md).

top_hidden._what: Part A of the top-of-file plan (explore/2026-10-29/top_research/PLAN.md, approved by John 29 October): the 2015 PUF's four aggregate records rebuilt as synthetic returns made from generated records (top_hidden.py says how). Nothing here changes training or the ordinary generation.
top_hidden._candidate_records: The extra batch of candidate filer records, by the 12 band-AGI label groups (qgroups.PUF_LABELS: below -$1M, -$1M to -$50k, -$50k to 0, below p50, ..., p99.5-99.9, p99.9-99.99, p99.99+), over all pooled models (each draws an equal share). Each candidate's weight is its group's 2015 PUF returns over the records drawn in it, so ranks counted in weight are population ranks. Groups left at 0 are not drawn: the aggregate records are returns with extreme items, which sit in the top three positive groups and the two loss groups.
top_hidden._candidate_seed: The candidates' generation seed (plus each model's seed_shift), apart from label_seed so no draw of the file moves.
top_hidden._selection: SOI's rule (Bryant, Czajka, Ivsin and Nunns 2014), counted in population weight: the top 400 returns by AGI; the 30 highest of each income item; the 30 lowest of each loss; the 10 highest (and, for fields with both signs, lowest) of most other amount fields. The fields of each rule are listed in top_hidden.py.
top_hidden._records_per_group: At most this many chosen records per aggregate group: a random sample with chance in proportion to the population weight, plus up to min_per_rule records of every selection rule the sample would otherwise lack.
top_hidden._targeted_per_gap: Where a group must have a sign of a field (its raw record's net amount needs it) and its chosen records have none, this many candidates outside the chosen set that have it (the largest first) are added.
top_hidden._count_tolerance: Each booklet count (returns with a positive, and with a negative, amount) is pulled toward the booklet's figure by the one-cost reweighting at tau 1 (solver.solve; top_hidden.py step 5), with the larger of this many returns and this share of the count as its standard error; each group's count of returns is an identity. The table of counts reports whether each count ends within that tolerance.
top_hidden._group_iterations: After the dollars are scaled, a record whose AGI has left its group is moved to the group its AGI is in (the first move_iterations rounds) or dropped (the later rounds), and the weights and the scaling are done again.
top_hidden._wealth: Step 7: every rebuilt return's balance sheet is drawn again under the SCF label given its final income items, up to wealth_tries times, until net worth in target-year dollars is below wealth_cap. Each try has its own network draws (wealth_seed and the try) and its own dollar picks keyed by record id (ages.uniform_by_id, wealth_salt). A record whose every try lands at or above the cap keeps its lowest try and is flagged (hidden_wealth_fallback).
top_hidden._id_block: Record ids of the rebuilt returns: id_block + 0, 1, ... (the generated file's models use 0 to 29,999,999).

consistency._what: Consistency rules at generation: when any item in when_any_nonzero is nonzero on the record, at least one holding in then_at_least_one_nonzero must be nonzero (generate.py says how). offset_generations: how many times generation runs; after each run but the last, each ruled holding's odds of being nonzero are scaled by one factor so that, with the rules, its expected holders equal the model's own. 1 means no offset.

rules.name: a partnership or S corporation item

dollars._what: seed: the seed of the draws that pick each record's dollars within its drawn band from the dollar map (dollars.py).
dollars._scf_caps: Balance-sheet items whose dollar map is held to a percentile among the wave's holders (weighted), in each SCF wave before it is grown to the target year (build_table.build_maps). Other debt: the SCF's largest amounts ($15-69 million) landed on ordinary records and one such record carried $0.27-0.92 trillion after the tilt; held to the 99.9th percentile among holders, $0.5-2.0 million (John, 28 October). The training table is unchanged, so the models are unaffected.

tilt._what: Post-training (tilt.py, solver.py, TARGETS.md): the start's weights scaled, then the weights moved to minimize one cost: the misses on every target in the year's list (targets_config/, expanded by target_list.py, each miss measured in its standard error from errors.py) plus the Kullback-Leibler size of the move (_reweighting says how). Which targets, their values and their errors are in targets_config/, not here.
tilt._prescale: The default start_scaling weights, when the year file gives none (target_list.start_spec): 'demographic' (TARGETS.md section 4): filers scaled to SOI's returns, then to Table 1.2's joint and non-joint returns, then to Table 1.6's returns by age range in each, and non-filers to the CPS's expected non-filers, then to the non-filer people targets, before the tilt; 'filing_status' stops after the joint and non-joint returns; 'none' scales filers and non-filers to their totals only.
tilt._precheck: precheck.py (1 November 2026): a check before the reweighting that only reports (precheck_flags.csv, precheck.md, the summary): a target is flagged when the average its count and amount require is outside the records' range by more than min_excess_se standard errors (rule 1), its relative standard error is below min_relative_se (rule 2), or the start is more than max_start_gap_se standard errors from it (rule 3). Nothing is dropped.
tilt._reweighting: The reweighting is one cost and no other rule (1 November 2026, decisions 57, 63, 64 and 68; solver.py). The file minimizes the sum over targets of 0.5 x importance x (miss / standard error)^2 plus tau x the Kullback-Leibler move of the weights from the start (in nats, on weights divided by the sum of the starting weights); identities are met exactly; no target has a range and none is dropped. The demographic prescaling uses the same rule on its cells. tau (1,000): the weight of the move against the misses; chosen in decision 63 (median miss 0.04 standard errors, 7 targets above 2 in 2022 on the new targets; the effective sample kept 62.5%). newton_budget: the most Newton steps in all (150 since 3 November, raised from 100 by John for 2023 with its Forbes list); never raised without John. gradient_tolerance: the solver's stopping size for the gradient of the dual, on the solver's scale (a miss as a share of the target's size). average_weight_change: an average's standard error is solved again at the first answer's group weight if a group moved by more than this share. importance_one_kinds: the target kinds with importance 1 (SOI's published tables, W-2 statistics, and the calculator's columns against SOI's); every other kind has importance 1 / other_importance_divisor.
tilt._projection: (3 November 2026, agent A; projection_steps.py) The projection years' three steps, used by a year whose targets.yaml has start_scaling {weights: persons, dollars: item_factor}. population_dir: CBO's Social Security area population by marital status and single year of age (Macro-Projections). items_table: one row per grown column, its growth series, kind, whether its total is targeted and its relative error (relative to the pipeline folder). add_factors_table (John, 3 November 2026): extra growth in percent a year on top of an item's series, one row per item and range of years (column, first_year, last_year, percent, note), compounding from the base year; applied in step 2, so the item's target total includes it; every non-zero percent needs a note (who, when, why); a header only means no add factors and the year is unchanged (relative to the pipeline folder). return_age_edges: the primary filer's age bands of the returns targets (under 20, 20-24, ..., 75-79, 80 and over). cbo_last_year (4 November 2026, the long-run years 2036-2075): the last year a CBO projection is used; after it every series continues at the growth of its long-run Macro-Projections aggregate (the items table's series files, resources/projection_long_run_mapping.csv; the growth.yaml rules and the count of returns, projection_growth.long_run_growth and returns_growth, resources/growth/macro_long_run.csv; resources/growth/build_long_run.py writes them), and CBO's counts of returns give no AMT target. item_min_records, item_min_dollars: a targeted item's gains (or losses) are a target only with at least this many records and this many 2023 dollars (Forbes list left out).
tilt._soft_cap: A soft cap on each record's final weight (1 November 2026, decision 62, John). U_i is k times the mean starting weight of the record's AGI group (nine groups, non-filers their own; records with a positive starting weight, held records left out; the mean since decision 73, John, 1 November: it was the median), and the cost gains 0.5 x beta x ((w_i - U_i)+ / U_i)^2 per record: no cost below U_i, quadratic above it. beta = x^2 makes a record at twice its cap cost as much as an x standard-error miss on a target of importance 1. beta = 1 is the mild strength (decision 68); beta = 100 held every record within 1.06 U in 2022 (decision 65). k null: no cap.
tilt._top: The very top of the file (PLAN.md of explore/2026-10-29/top_research, approved by John 29 October; top_records.py, top_billionaires.py). enabled: the preparation step runs in tilt.main before any mask, condition or prescaling, and the SCF targets' population (catalog scf_units_below_a_billion) is the units below $1 billion of net worth, in the SCF and in the file; false: none of it, the SCF targets on every unit and Table 4.3's top 0.001% left out (target_list.expand drops the must_reach cells), as before. billionaire_lists: the year's Forbes list in research/rebuild/resources/top (tax year t uses the March or April list of year t, 2015-2026 since 2 November 2026, built by resources/top/build_forbes.py; its records have weight 1, held fixed; a year with none: no billionaires, and a warning). after_last_list.grow (John, 2 November 2026): a year after the last list takes the last list grown to the year (top_billionaires.grow_list: each fortune's public stock, private business and real estate grown as the projection start grows value.equities, value.pass_throughs and value.re_fund; income from the IRS study's ratios as in a list year; ages raised), its records starting at weight 1 times their cell's population growth from the list's year. after_last_list.fixed (2 November 2026, a placeholder until the projection years are redesigned; John called the projection targeting a disaster to be redesigned): true holds those records at their starting weight in the solver, as the list years hold theirs at 1; false leaves them free under the soft cap, which in the 2 November run (explore/2026-11-02/billionaires/RESULTS.md) sent the ten richest to weights near zero. hidden_returns: Part A (top_hidden.py, merged 29 October; generated starts only; its build is cached in <gen>/hidden). redraw_tries: tries per generated record whose net worth comes out at $1 billion or more (top_billionaires.redraw_record, the same function Part A's rebuilt returns use with settings top_hidden.wealth_*; the tries drawn as one batch from generators seeded by redraw_seed and the record id, the dollar picks keyed by the record id and redraw_salt); if every try is at or above $1 billion the lowest is kept and flagged (open question 2: 20 chosen, the fallback rate reported). stand_in_agi, stand_in_min_records: without Part A's rebuilt over-$100-million group (hidden_group 3; mix_from_hidden), the billionaires' item mix comes from the generated filers with AGI at or above this (target-year dollars), or the top 0.01% if fewer records. gift_rate_top, gift_rate_rest: gifts as a share of wealth, BSYZ (2025) Table 2's top 100 and next 300.

non_micro_imputations._what: The non-microdata imputations (non_micro_imputations.py; NEXT_STEPS.md item 1, John's decisions Q1-Q9 of 28 October; FEATURES.md): items set from what the model has drawn plus a published table, no new microdata. Each item: the columns it reads, the published tables it reads (research/rebuild/resources/non_micro/, built by build_non_micro_tables.py; sources.csv there), the columns it writes and its random stream. They run inside the tilt stage on the start (target-year dollars, prescaled weights), before the solve; the two ranking items rank on the start's weights. Each item writes new columns only and never changes a drawn item or a weight, except that a primary filer with an age and no sex is given a sex first (fill_missing_sex), and an item may change a drawn column it lists in writes_back (column: the new column that keeps the drawn value; only amt_nol_cap does). Their published checks are reported only (Q9), in report.md section 6 and non_micro_checks.md.
non_micro_imputations._salt_base: Every random number is ages.uniform_by_id(record_id, salt_base + 8 x stream + person), person 0 for the unit, 1 and 2 for the primary filer and the spouse, 3 to 5 for dependents 1 to 3: a fixed function of the record, the stream and the person, so it never moves when other code or other records change. Streams are numbered once in the items below and never renumbered. Stream 3 (the placeholder for dependents' Social Security numbers until 29 October) is no longer used: the numbers come from the model's draws (dollars.py).

dependent_filer_age_sex._why: Q2 (John, 28 October): each dependent filer (the PUF's three dependent-filer age ranges) gets an exact age and a sex drawn from the CPS dependents the filing stage counts as filing their own return (p_own_return 1), in the record's own CPS year, within the record's age range; the draw keyed by record id. This pool dates from 2 November 2026 (John; explore/2026-11-02/dependent_filers/RESULTS.md). Before then the pool was the dependents with earnings (wages and self-employment) above the year's dependent filing threshold, with the filing stage's rule as a fallback for a range with fewer than 30 sample people (26 and over); that pool was 64-83% age 18 within 18-25, because under the CPS tax-unit rule few dependents aged 19-23 earn above the threshold, while the filing pool is 37-46% age 18. The old rule was taken out of the code on 3 November 2026 (the simplification; it is in the git history). Ages above top_age are put at top_age (80 means 80 and over, as for the primary filer). dep_filer_age is -1 and dep_filer_sex 0 on every other record.

child_credit._why: Production's rule (src/imputations/ages.R): dependent k (youngest first) passes every child credit test except age and Social Security number when it is under 17 and the record's n_dep_ctc (the PUF's count of child credit children, 2015 law) is at least k; dependents from 17 to the year's law age less one (17 alone in every year but 2021) pass by chance, 1 - the share of units with dependents under 17 whose count of them exceeds n_dep_ctc (start weights), as production. 1 passes, 0 not, -1 no such dependent. Tax-Simulator applies the age limit of the law it simulates.

death_probabilities._why: Production's three layers (src/mortality_ledger.R), no draw: the SSA period life table for the year, age and sex (80 means 80 and over: the average of q over ages 80-119 weighted by the table's L); times Chetty et al.'s mortality ratio at the person's percentile of broad income within sex and single age (start weights); times, for men only, Johnson et al.'s married or unmarried factor, rescaled to average 1 on the file within under 65 and 65 and over. Dependent filers use their ages and sex from dependent_filer_age_sex. q_death2 is -1 without a spouse. Stream 8 only for primary filers whom generation gave an age but no sex (2 records on 28 October): a sex with even chances, written back to sex_primary before any item runs (fill_missing_sex; the one drawn column this module changes; generate.py now forces the primary filer's sex to a man or a woman).

unrealized_gains._why: Q6 (John, 28 October): one column per asset, value x the year's Z.1 revaluation rate (households and nonprofits): stocks at the corporate equities rate, businesses at noncorporate business equity's, the three kinds of real estate at real estate's, trusts at 60% stocks and 40% bonds (debt securities), retirement accounts at a stock share x the stocks rate + the rest x the bonds rate. Years with no full year of Z.1 data take production's long-run rates (bonds 0). The retirement accounts' stock share is the SCF's (w_dc_stock_share, RETEQ / RETQLIQ, learned in pretraining and drawn with the balance sheet since 29 October). A file from a model before then has no such draw, and the stage stops on it (until 3 November 2026 such a file used production's age rule, 1.10 - age of the older adult / 100 held to 0.20-0.95).

cost_basis._why: Production's rule (src/imputations/wealth.R, to_output_schema): basis = value - the SCF's unrealized gain; the gain on other real estate is split between other homes and other real estate by value (half each when both are zero). Each gain is first held to no more than the value, so a basis is never below 0 (John, 28 October; the gain and the value are drawn separately, so a gain could exceed the value).

gains_holding_period._why: Q7 (John, 28 October): production's method (src/imputations/capital_gains.R). A holding-period group drawn with SOCA's share of long-term gain dollars (loss dollars for losses), an exact period in the group from a Weibull shape (an exponential tail above 20 years); basis from production's regression on SOCA's panel, log(basis/sales) = a constant per group + b x years x log(1 + trailing S&P 500 return), evaluated at the target year's trailing returns (past the index's last year, the index grows at its 1926-last geometric mean). Person 1 picks the group, person 2 the period. kg_lt_years_held is -1 and kg_lt_basis 0 where kg_lt is 0. Each period is held to at most the older adult's age less 18, and at least 1 year (John, 28 October; the basis is computed at the held period).

reads: the income items of production's measure
parents_rank._why: Q8 (John, 28 October): production's method (src/imputations/mobility.R): each unit's income ranked among all units in percentiles (start weights), the bottom 10 merged into rank 10, then a parent rank drawn from Chetty et al.'s matrix. Production's code sends the bottom 9% to rank 100 (cut() gives them no group, replace_na(100)); the rebuild follows the code's stated intent (rank 10).

blindness._why: Q3 as a rule (John, second retrain of 29 October): for each primary filer, and each spouse on a married-joint record, a draw keyed by record id and person, blind with chance = the 2015 PUF's blind rate for the person's age range (where the return shows it) times one factor per person type; each factor makes the filers' weighted count at the start's weights equal Publication 4801's blind boxes for the target year. Non-filers are drawn by the same rule and not counted. Replaces the PUF slot learned in pretraining (29 October), whose draws were ten times too many.

reads: the partnership and S corporation parts
qbi._why: Q5 (John, 28 October; scratch explore/2026-10-28/qbi_plan/SIMPLE_PLAN.md; built 29 October). For each record and kind (Schedule C, partnership, S corporation) with positive income of that kind: specified service drawn (person 1-3 by kind) with chance b x c(group), at most 1, the group the model drew for the kind (an SCF item learned in pretraining); wage bill = a x the drawn owner's share of outside workers x the CPS's average pay of private employees in the group in the target year, plus, for an S corporation, all the record's wages when it has S corporation income and no Schedule C or partnership income (first version). Group 8 (no industry code): c is the average of groups 1-7 weighted by positive income on the file, pay is all private employees'. Farms: never specified service, wage bill = positive farm income. c_by_scf_group: the plan's table (Treasury's Form 8995-A shares by detailed industry, Goodman, Lim, Sacerdote and Whitten Table A1, averaged within each SCF group over CPS self-employed people 2017-2019). a and b: the two dials' starting values. Since 30 October every tilt solves them on the start's weights, against Treasury's share (a) and SOI Table 1.4's deduction (b) (taxes.solve_qbi_dials, settings taxes.qbi_dials; a is held at 1 by its range); a year without SOI's QBI line carries the dials of the file its start comes from, or else uses these values. Changing a, b or c needs only a rerun of the tilt stage. No QBI targets.

amt_nol_cap._why: John, 29 October. The AMT net operating loss adjustment (amt_nols, the PUF's P60100) is held to at most the record's net operating loss, and is 0 on a record with no loss. The loss is the negative part of other_agi_remainder: the PUF has no field of its own for it, and a net operating loss deduction is reported as a negative amount in other income (Form 1040 line 21), which is in the AGI remainder. A negative amt_nols is left as drawn. The model draws amt_nols and the remainder separately, so a record could carry a large AMT adjustment with no loss behind it (the calculator experiment of 28 October: AMT five times SOI's from such records). The rule changes a drawn column (writes_back); the drawn value is kept as amt_nols_drawn. amt_nols is in PUF-year dollars (no Table 1.4 line), the loss in target-year dollars; they are compared as they are. No target reads amt_nols, so the rule moves no weight.

errors._what: Standard errors (errors.py, TARGETS.md section 9). Every setting here is optional, with the default given; none is set today.
errors._scf_replicate_dir: The folder of each SCF wave's replicate weights (p<yy>_rw1.dta, from the Federal Reserve; errors.py says how to fetch them), with {wave} in the path for the wave. Default: <out>/data/scf_rw/{wave}, which holds the 2016, 2019 and 2022 waves' files. Every wave in a year's mix needs its folder (scf_targets.py).
errors._other: soi_cv_dir (default <out>/targets/soi_cv), borrow_neighbours (5), full_sample_se (0.01), full_sample_cv_below_pct (0.1: a published CV below this many percent is treated like the printed 0.00, sampled in full, decision 55), nonfiler_people_population_se (0.005): errors.py's docstring says what each means.

_targets_config: Optional key targets_config: a folder holding a copy of targets_config/ (catalog.yaml and one folder per year, <year>/targets.yaml, prior.yaml and growth.yaml) to read instead of the pipeline's own, for a reweighting variant (target_list.py, growth.py, config_overview.py). Absent: pipeline/targets_config.

taxes._what: Taxes computed inside the model (taxes.py; piece 3 of the overnight plan of 29-30 October; design: scratch explore/2026-10-22/targets/calculator_api/REPORT.md). Inside the tilt stage, on the start after the top of the file and the non-microdata imputations and before the reweighting, every record's taxes under the target year's law from tax-simulator-gpu's batch command (python -m taxmodel.run.batch, on its local branch taxdata-batch-1103: master 080b8dbb of 3 November with the batch command and the itemized deduction categories added, not pushed), from a copy of that repository at commit (git archive into <out>/lib/tax-simulator-gpu_<first 12 characters>), run with its own Python environment (python). The computed columns (taxes.OUTPUTS, each the calculator's name with calc_ in front) join the file by record id, and the year's calculator targets (kind calculator in targets_config/) read them. Replaces the calculator experiment's own runner (calculator_run.py, 28 October); the stage calculator now calls the same command.
taxes._target: true: the year's calculator targets join the reweighting; false: they are only reported (taxes/taxes_fit.csv, before and after a tilt without them).
taxes._draw_seed: The seed of the calculator's random draws keyed by record id (its default run seed, 76): the child care credit's take-up, the state tax workaround's owners and the others.
taxes._law_year: The year of the law the taxes are computed under; null: the target year. tax-simulator-gpu compiles the law of 2014 to 2040 (checked 29 October; 2013 fails).
taxes._law_alternative: null: the default law folder (current law as enacted: TCJA, the 2020-21 measures, OBBBA). Else a folder under the calculator's config/scenarios/tax_law/alternatives.
taxes._wage_increment: Dollars added to the primary earner's wages for the marginal rates on wages (calc_mtr_wages_iit, calc_mtr_wages_payroll); 0: not computed.
taxes._refund_rule: Decision 47 (John, 30 October): after the draw, a record the calculator says does not itemize under the year's law (one calculator run on the grown start, the flag itemizing) has its taxable state income tax refund (state_ref) set to zero. It stands in for 'did not itemize last year'. A rule like the AMT rule: the draw carries 2015's roughly 21 million refund returns into every year, and SOI has 4.3 million in 2019 and 3.1 million in 2023. false: the draw's refunds stay.

greedy_schedule_a._what: Decision 49 (John, 30 October; design ALGO_GROWTH_SEARCH.md, the simple version): in a year with a Table 2.1 (2015-2023), after the growth by the declared priors and the refund rule, each category's input factor s (medical: med_exp; taxes paid: salt_inc_sales and salt_prop; interest: first_mort_int; charity: char_cash and char_noncash) is set so that the start's dollars per claiming return (the calculator's claimed amount over the filer returns claiming it, at the start's weights, all AGI) match Table 2.1's (its amounts over its counts, all AGI groups). passes: calculator runs, each followed by a multiplicative update of s; max_move: s stays within one plus or minus this of the prior (s = 1). Other itemized deductions keep the prior (Table 2.1 has no count for the residual). Years without a Table 2.1 (the chained years from 2024) keep the priors.

qbi_dials._what: SIMPLE_PLAN.md step 4 (scratch explore/2026-10-28/qbi_plan): the QBI dials a (wage bill) and b (specified service) of non_micro_imputations.items.qbi, solved on the start's weights before the reweighting (taxes.solve_qbi_dials). a: owners of exactly one business (Schedule C, partnership or S corporation, no farm income) that is not a specified service, with taxable income above the top of the phase-in range, keep Treasury's share of 20% of their business income; b: the deduction on returns with AGI of soi_agi_floor or more equals SOI Table 1.4's. Solved in turn, at most rounds times, each by bisection in its range. false: a and b stay at the settings' values (1).
qbi_dials._treasury_share_by_scf_group: Goodman, Lim, Sacerdote and Whitten, NBER Working Paper 28680 (revised January 2024), Table A1, column 1: actual 2018-2019 returns, owners of one business with taxable income above the phase-in range, the deduction as a share of 20% of potential QBI, in the industries that are not specified services. By SCF industry group (the Census codes of build_non_micro_tables.SCF_INDUSTRY_RANGES): 2 construction of buildings 0.68; 3 manufacturing 0.76 and publishers 0.65; 4 wholesale 0.59 and restaurants 0.84. A group's value is the average of its industries; the target is the groups' values weighted by the file's business income of those owners in each group. Groups 1, 5, 6, 7 and 8 have no published industry.
qbi_dials._a_range: The range the wage dial a is searched in. Held at 1 since 30 October (the overnight run, decision 30 of explore/2026-10-30/DECISIONS_FOR_JOHN.md): on the installed networks the solve gave a = 3.00, wage bills nearly twice the economy's private wages; on the new networks it ran to the top of [0, 20] without reaching Treasury's share (0.66 against 0.70) and made wage bills of $84 trillion. The cause: most high-income owners of one business have no outside workers drawn, so no a gives them a wage bill. [0, 20] restores the solve; b is still solved.
